{{Short description|British mathematician (1896–1973)}}

{{Use dmy dates|date=August 2019}}
'''William Reginald Dean''' (1896–1973) was a British [[Applied mathematics|applied mathematician]] and [[Fluid dynamics|fluid dynamicist]]. His research interests included [[Stokes flow]], [[solid mechanics]], and flow in curved channels. The [[Dean number]] bears his name.

Dean carried out pioneering work in the study of fluid flow at low [[Reynolds number]]s, by applying methods from [[elasticity theory]]. Some of his more famous results include solutions for secondary flow in curved tubes, for the perturbation to shear flow near a wall caused by a gap in the wall, and for flow in a corner.<ref name="binnie78">{{cite journal | last1 = Binnie | first1 = A. M. | year = 1978 | title = Some Notes on the Study of Fluid Mechanics in Cambridge, England | journal = Annual Review of Fluid Mechanics | volume = 10 | pages = 1–11 | doi = 10.1146/annurev.fl.10.010178.000245 |bibcode = 1978AnRFM..10....1B | doi-access = free }}</ref>

Dean was an undergraduate at [[Trinity College, Cambridge]]. He spent five years at [[Imperial College London|Imperial College]], and was later a fellow of Trinity College. During the war he undertook mathematical work as part of the ''Anti-Aircraft Experimental Section of M.I.D.''<ref>{{cite journal | doi = 10.1098/rsbm.1945.0005  | doi-access = free| last1 = Milne | first1 = E. A. | year = 1945 | title = Ralph Howard Fowler. 1889-1944 | journal = Obituary Notices of Fellows of the Royal Society | volume = 5 | issue = 14| pages = 60–78 | bibcode = 1945ApJ...101....1C | s2cid = 170967451 }}</ref> He also held the Goldsmid Chair in Applied Mathematics at [[University College London]] (from which he retired in 1964),<ref>{{cite journal | doi = 10.1098/rsbm.1985.0019  | doi-access = free| last1 = Lighthill | first1 = J. | year = 1985 | title = Keith Stewartson: 20 September 1925 &ndash; 7 May 1983 | journal = Biographical Memoirs of Fellows of the Royal Society | volume = 31 | pages = 544–569 | jstor=769936}}</ref> and a chair at the [[University of Arizona]].<ref name="binnie78" />
